choices.why: gnōmon = sundial-pointer; Origen appeals to contemporary shadow science, including shadowless (tropical) gnomons — keep the period term.
aideomai = shame/reverence; the soul-bride's beauty shames bodily comparison — Origen's ascent logic.
Distinct rank-title beside archangels/thrones/dominions; transliteration preserves the catalog.

pass_a_gloss: Unequal shadows prove unequal bodily concomitants: as gnomons cast none, short, or long shadows by ineffable analogies, so prior gifts draw varied shadows; the sun-seeker ignores shadows, and the enlightened ignore material trivialities beside saving gifts. Bodily wealth, flesh-health, bodily beauty (grass-flower), earthly nobility and kingdom all collapse before soul-beauty, sonship, the unshakable kingdom, and the angelic orders; pray the prior things and leave shadows to the God who knows need before asking.
pass_b_english: It is no wonder that, just as not the same shadow is given to all who receive, so to speak, the bodies that make such shadows — to some no shadow at all, to others the same shadow — so too with the prior gifts. For this is plainly seen to hold for bodies as well by those who study gnomonic problems and the ratio of shadows to the illuminating body: for gnomons are shadowless at certain seasons, and others have, so to speak, short shadows, and others longer shadows than others. It is no great thing, then, if — since the purpose of the giver who grants the prior gifts fits them by certain ineffable and mystical analogies to the receivers and to the times when the prior gifts are given — at one time no shadows at all follow the receivers, at another not all but few, at another lesser ones by comparison, with greater ones following others. As, then, one who seeks the sun's rays is neither gladdened nor grieved by the presence or absence of the bodies' shadow, having the most necessary thing — whether enlightened or deprived of the shadow, or having more or less of the shadow — so, if the spiritual gifts are with us and we are enlightened by God toward the complete possession of the true goods, we shall not fuss over a cheap matter of shadow. For all material and bodily things, whatever they may be, have the worth of a faint and feeble shadow, wholly unable to be compared with the saving and holy gifts of the God of all. For what comparison is there of bodily wealth with the wealth 'in all speech' and 'all' wisdom?

And who but a madman would compare health of flesh and bones with a healthy and vigorous soul and well-measured reasonings? All of which, ordered by the word of God, make bodily sufferings some cheap scratch — even if we count the scratch briefer than it is. But he who has contemplated what the beauty of the bride is, whose 'songs' the word of God loves — a soul in bloom with supercelestial and supermundane beauty — will be ashamed to honor with the same name of beauty the bodily beauty of woman or boy or ... Flesh is as grass, and its 'glory,' which appears in what is called the beauty of women and children, has been likened by the prophetic word to a flower, saying: 'All flesh is as grass, and all its glory as the flower of grass. The grass is withered, and the flower fallen; but the word of the Lord abides forever.' (1 Corinthians 1:5) But who will properly call nobility the trite thing called so among men, who has conceived the nobility of sons of God? And the mind that has contemplated Christ's 'unshakable' kingdom — how will it not despise as worth nothing 'all the kingdom upon earth' (Isaiah 40:6–8)? And having seen, as far as a human mind still bound in body can hold, and grasped as far as possible, the army of angels and archistrategi — among them powers of the Lord, archangels and thrones and dominions and principalities and authorities, supercelestial — how will it not, even if feebler than a shadow, despise as dimmest, comparing them, even these things admired among the senseless as worth no account, even if all these are given — and overlook them all, for the sake of not missing the true principalities and the more divine authorities? We must pray, then, pray concerning the prior and truly great and heavenly things, and leave the matters of the shadows that follow the prior things to God, who knows 'what need' we have, through the mortal body, 'before' we ask him (Hebrews 12:28) (Colossians 1:16 (thrones) (Matthew 6:8) (Colossians 1:16).
